newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar turns lower in pre-expiry trade.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar turns lower in pre-expiry trade.

text.p: London's May white sugar contract tumbled over $4.00 in solid Monday trading with the weakness blamed on pre-expiry book-squaring and the downward correction in the New York market.
By 1545 GMT both nearby positions had bounced up from their session lows but the dive on the spot month dragged the May/August spread into a discount from a premium of more than $2.00 last week.
May was down $4.10 at $307.70 and August down $2.10 at $308.70. Other months also lost ground.
"It's all expiry stuff...but it looks shaky," said one trader. Volume totalled 3,844 lots.
As expected, New York saw a sell-off from last week's highs, although May raws halted its decline at a low of 11.12 cents/lb as buying from trade shorts kicked in.
In London, activity was dominated by the standard rolling of spot positions into the further forward months with commission houses and other brokers featuring on both sides of the market.
Traders said the May/May arbitrage was attracting very little buying interest, even at the lower levels.
"There hasn't been a rush at it," said one.
"It's narrowed down and I would have thought that people who were very short might have come in and rushed at it," he said.

Other market sources said the reluctance of short holders to move out of the May contract suggested that a high delivery could be on the cards, possibly as much as 10 cargoes of European origin sugars.
Paris nearby positions were also lower but Matif volume stayed on the light side at 245 lots.
May was down $3.00 at $309.50 and August down $1.50 at $308.50.
